system.description:
You build your armour rather than buy it: a suit that carries your Spark Caster in its gauntlets. Taught at Tenor Hold, where the rifles are made, and among Eltor's war-smiths.

Reshapes: your Spark Caster becomes the suit's weapons.

Gauntlets: while you wear the suit, your Spark Caster is built into its gauntlets and your hands stay free. The gauntlets come off the suit: worn alone they are your Spark Caster, with no model.

Model: choose the suit's model during each long rest. With Quick Hands you may switch between the two as part of firing.

Bulwark: when you fire at a creature within 5ft, you can make it a Fortitude save for thunder damage, still half on a success. If it fails, it has Disadvantage on attacks against anyone but you until the start of your next turn.

Ghost: your Spark Caster reaches 120ft, and the suit loses the Noisy trait.

Suit mods: the suit carries one suit mod (two from 3rd), chosen from your known options (see Armourer: Known Suit Mods) and swapped during a rest. Turning one on for the day costs 1 Ingenuity Point.

  • Built Suit (1st): You are trained in all heavy armour, but not in shields.
  • You start with a Chain Mail Hauberk reworked as your built suit.
  • During a long rest you may rework another suit you own into your built suit; you have one at a time, reworking another ends the first (and any permanent suit mod in it), and a magic suit keeps its own properties.
  • Only you can wear it.
  • Suit Mods (3rd): The suit carries two suit mods.
  • Reinforced Frame (5th): The suit gives +1 AC and Resistance 5 to one of acid, cold, fire, lightning or thunder. Choose it when you rework the suit; you can change it during a long rest.
  • Integrated Arms (7th): When you fire the Spark Caster, spend 1 Ingenuity Point to fire the other gauntlet too, at the same or another target in range. The second shot is a separate save, uses the same model and adds no Intelligence modifier.
  • Lasting Work: Masterwork Suit (10th): As often as Lasting Work allows, spend a full day and materials (see Lasting Work) to make one suit mod permanent.
  • A permanent mod costs no Ingenuity Points and doesn't count against the mods the suit carries; a suit holds one permanent mod, two from 15th.
  • You may instead make a mod permanent on an ally's armour.
  • Name the suit and give it a line of history: you are its maker.
  • Great Work (20th): The Walking Fortress: your suit carries every suit mod you know, at no cost. Once per encounter, when you drop to 0 HP, the suit keeps you standing at 1 HP. Requires a month of uninterrupted work and materials as for Lasting Work.

Known Suit Mods

  • Guardian Plating: The suit grants +2 AC.
  • Featherweight: The suit takes half its slots (round up) and loses the Cumbersome trait.
  • Ward-Etched: The suit adds +1 to all saving throws.
  • Glowing Ward: The suit sheds light in a 30ft radius, and you gain Advantage on saves vs fear.
  • Silent Step: Advantage on checks to move silently (with Bulwark it only cancels the Noisy trait).
  • Grasping Claw: Advantage on grapple attempts.
  • Lantern Core: Light in a 30ft radius or a 60ft beam, shuttered at will; it also burns under water and in wind.
  • Climbing Spikes: A climb speed equal to your speed; the suit's Cumbersome trait doesn't apply to climbing.
  • Alarm Core: While you wear the suit, add +5 to your passive awareness against surprise.
  • Storage Cavity: A hidden compartment holding up to 4 slots of items, which don't count against your slots.
  • Guardian Plating and Ward-Etched don't add to a magic suit's own bonus: use the higher. An Armourer's known options beyond these ten are custom designs (see Reverse Engineer).
